reason: Connect the retort to hydrogen to prepare it for processing the iron-rich feedstock.
expectation: I expect a hydrogen-fed retort; it may still need feedstock and further processing before producing iron.

alternatives.reason: The cable and steel may be useful for equipment, but the retort seems more directly tied to the current goal.

effect: The retort now has heat and hydrogen but still needs concentrate; the remaining combination may help prepare it.
reaction: The contained exhaust and condensate make the setup feel practical, though the next connection is not yet clear.
reason: This is the only offered gameplay action, so I’ll use the cable and steel to make whatever equipment they support.
expectation: I expect some powered workshop component, but I’m unsure how it will help prepare the concentrate.

effect: The cable and steel made a switchable magnetic separator, giving me a way to concentrate grains from the screened regolith.
reaction: The explanation of switching off the magnet to release the grains is useful and clear.
reason: Use the separator on the regolith to prepare feedstock for the retort; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect it to collect a magnetic, iron-rich fraction, though it may need further processing before it becomes usable iron.

effect: The separator produced an assayed iron-rich concentrate ready for the hydrogen-fed retort.
reaction: The distinction between the red colour and the mineral assay is a useful detail.
reason: Feed the concentrate into the retort to work toward usable iron; this is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect heat and hydrogen to reduce the iron-bearing minerals, though the resulting material may need further processing.

effect: The retort produced porous, weak reduced iron that needs further processing at the press.
reaction: The explanation of hydrogen removing oxygen makes the reduction clear.
reason: Press the iron sponge toward a usable form; this is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect a denser iron form, though I’m unsure whether pressing alone will make it usable.

effect: The heated press consolidated the sponge into a dense billet, and the next goal is to shape a process frame.
reaction: The distinction between consolidating iron and shaping a part is clear and useful.
reason: Use the press again to shape the billet into the needed frame; this is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the press to form a frame or a frame component from the consolidated iron.

effect: The press shaped the billet into non-pressure supports suitable for the process frame.
reaction: The distinction between supports and flight hardware is reassuringly clear.
reason: Fit the bars and brackets to the return-plant footing to make the frame; this is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect a supported process frame on the prepared footing, though it may still need equipment installed.

effect: The local iron supports now form a process frame on the prepared footing, completing the chapter’s goals; the gas installation remains for later.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the processed material become a tangible structure, while the precision vessel remains imported.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reducing the concentrate with hydrogen was most worthwhile: it explained how oxygen is removed and produced a visibly different, porous material that still needed consolidation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Shaping and mounting the supports felt like straightforward finishing steps rather than meaningful decisions, although they gave the process a concrete result.

surprise.text: The cable and steel made a switchable electromagnet for separating the feedstock; its purpose was not clear to me when I chose the combination.

arbitrary.text: The cable-and-steel combination initially lacked a clear purpose, especially as the only offered action. The separator result explained it afterward.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see the gas installation fitted and how the local-propellant return plan develops; the material-processing explanations made this chapter worthwhile despite its mostly forced choices.
